subject.title: fix(code-mode): preserve concurrent tool execution safely

question: Should Code Mode preserve every dispatched race or detached tool call through terminal draining even when the guest’s top-level Promise has already resolved?
rationale: This is a runtime-semantics and latency/cancellation tradeoff in an agent execution path; the patch’s stated intent is plausible, but the permanent product contract should be confirmed by the responsible maintainer.

options.title: Adopt drain-all semantics
options.body: Approve retaining and draining every dispatched request so detached side effects complete, with explicit real-worker proof of the resulting latency and cancellation behavior.

options.title: Limit draining to owned requests
options.body: Require a narrower protocol that identifies only requests still needed by the guest’s terminal computation, accepting that detached side effects may need a separate contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt drain-all semantics
recommendation.body: Approve retaining and draining every dispatched request so detached side effects complete, with explicit real-worker proof of the resulting latency and cancellation behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context connects this person directly to the proposed execution-contract change, though current-main ownership history was not independently established.
